subtitle: BizHawk

description: Dracula's castle as a multiworld. DSS cards, relics and movement abilities are shuffled across the session, so how far into the castle you can reach depends on the whole group.
_description_source: written by us from the structure of the game - no text copied from the game itself
_checks_verified_note: Stays false until the RAM map has been MEASURED in-game. Until then London warns at launch.
_requires_source: GBA title - the game lives on a cartridge the player owns

rom.description: A Castlevania: Circle of the Moon ROM of the US version specifically -- either the original cartridge dump or the Castlevania Advance Collection rip
rom._description_source: world source: ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago worlds/cvcotm (upstream), read from the world's own code
rom._size_note: Not measured. London reads size 0 as 'unknown' and matches on MD5 alone, which is the stronger check.
rom._md5_source: world source: ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago worlds/cvcotm (upstream), read from the world's own code -- the accepted-dump list the world validates the player's file against

apworld._source: game list plus the world's own repository

patch._source: audit_patch_model.py read the world: cvcotm/rom.pyc: class CVCotMProcedurePatch(APProcedurePatch)

_note: rom.py lists a third hash for the Wii U Virtual Console dump but has it COMMENTED OUT, so it is deliberately not accepted.
_lua_module_source: filename under Multiworld-Launcher/Plugins/Scripts/games/ — the modules predate this catalogue and use their own short names

world_by.name: the Archipelago project and its contributors
world_by._source: this world ships with Archipelago itself (apworld.bundled)
world_by._licence_source: read from ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago's own LICENSE file, 2026-08-19 -- the MIT text; GitHub's classifier says 'Other' because the file carries extra wording, so the body was read rather than the label
world_by._authors_source: read from worlds/cvcotm/__init__.py in ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago -- the names the world itself publishes in its WebWorld tutorial credits. These are credited for the world's guide, which is usually but not always the same people who wrote the world; the licence holder above is unchanged.

credits._note: The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its author's work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.
